So `Output` gets `id`, computed in strand-services' snapshot from a copy of `identity_description` (strand-services does not depend on strand-surface; a unit test in crates/strand, `services::output_id::an_outputs_id_is_its_screens_id`, holds the copy equal to `MonitorId`). Two findings from headless sway (`screens_focus.rs::an_outputs_id_is_its_screens_id_on_sway`): the output-management head gives no make or model where `wl_output` says `Unknown` (wlroots' `wl_output` default), so an empty make or model is `Unknown` in the id; and the descriptions agree. Identical heads are numbered with the ones on first, in the compositor's order, then the ones off: strand-surface numbers in `wl_output` plug order among monitors shown, and a monitor off has no `wl_output`, so this agrees for every monitor shown, and an off one still has an id a profile can name. Which of two identical monitors is `#2` can change across restarts, as for `Screen.id`. Not verified on Hyprland or niri (no matrix run in this stream): a compositor whose head and `wl_output` disagree on make or description would give ids that differ there, which the headless test would show for sway only.

**2026-11-07 · output-id review round 1: an output keeps its id while it is there.** `number_ids` numbered identical monitors statelessly, the ones on first, so turning one of two identical monitors off swapped their ids: a profile `X` off, `X #2` on, applied, renamed them and was applied again every 1.5 s, and a hotplug gave a monitor another `#n` than its `Screen.id`, which strand-surface keeps across plugs. Each head now keeps the id it had at the last snapshot (`HeadEntry::id`): those on keep theirs first, a new one or one turned on whose id another monitor on holds takes the lowest number no monitor on holds (as `Monitors::plug` reclaims an unplugged record), and one off takes what no other output holds; a new set is numbered as before, those on first. Which of two identical monitors is `#2` can still change across a restart of Strand, as `Screen.id` can. That `Output.id` equals `Screen.id` on Hyprland is still unchecked (nested Hyprland was not run for it). Test: `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::an_identical_monitor_keeps_its_id_while_it_is_there`. (Review round 2:) a monitor turned on since the last snapshot comes to `number_ids` with no id, so it takes the lowest number no monitor on holds, as the new `wl_output` it gets is numbered by `Monitors::plug`: with two identical monitors both off, the one turned on is the unnumbered one in both lists (it had kept its ` #2`, so the two lists disagreed). Same test, and `turned_on_afresh`. Run on nested Hyprland 0.57 for the first time, the two ids disagreed: its `wl_output` sends an empty make and model (headless outputs), which `Screen.id` kept empty while `Output.id` wrote `Unknown`, as wlroots' `wl_output` says it on sway. strand-surface's `MonitorId::new` now writes an empty make or model `Unknown` too, so both read `Unknown | Unknown | ` (and ` #2`) there; sway is unchanged, its `wl_output` already saying `Unknown` (`crates/strand/src/services/mod.rs::output_id::an_outputs_id_is_its_screens_id`, with Hyprland's empty case). Checked by hand with `scripts/container/hyprland-nested.sh` (a `file` writing both lists); a real monitor's description on Hyprland, which headless outputs do not give, is still unchecked.

**2026-11-07 · output-id review round 3: an output keeps its id while it is connected, and `Screen.id` takes its number from `outputs`.** Round 2's `turned_on_afresh` (a monitor turned on took the lowest number no monitor on held, to match `Monitors::plug`) brought back round 1's loop: two identical monitors with no serial, DP-2 on as `X` and DP-1 off as `X #2`, and a profile `X` off, `X #2` on; applied, DP-1 came on as `X` and DP-2 went off as `X #2`, so the profile named the other pair and was applied again every 1.5 s. Rounds 1 and 2 each fixed one side of a conflict that cannot be fixed in `outputs` alone: strand-surface sees a monitor only while it is on (a monitor off has no `wl_output`), so its plug numbering cannot know that a monitor off is still connected and holds a number, and which number a monitor turned on gets depended on whether the compositor removed the other's `wl_output` first. The rule, written down before the code: (1) a connected monitor keeps its `Output.id` for as long as it is connected, on or off, so applying a configuration, which connects and disconnects nothing, renames nothing, and a profile chosen by id is still the one chosen after it is applied (no loop, whatever the profile); (2) a monitor plugged in takes the lowest number no connected monitor of its identity holds, those on first in the compositor's order, then those off (a new set at start, as before); (3) `Screen.id` follows `Output.id`, never the reverse: `Monitors::plug` takes the number the last `outputs` snapshot gave its connector (`SurfaceHost::output_ids`, the binary's host reading `strand_services::outputs::ids()`, a process-wide list of connector and id for every monitor connected), and without one (no `outputs` service, or a monitor plugged in before its head is published) the lowest number no monitor plugged in holds and the list gives no other connector, which is rule 2 again. The list outlives a run of `outputs`, so a run restarted after an error gives its heads the ids the last one gave their connectors. Left as they were: two identical monitors plugged in at the same moment are numbered in the order each side sees them; with no `outputs` service in the config, `Screen.id` is numbered by plug order alone, as before; which of two is ` #2` can change when Strand restarts. Tests, each failing without the fix: `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::a_profile_that_swaps_identical_monitors_is_applied_once` (the profile above through `Client::snapshot`, applied once and then never again; both monitors turned off and on in the other order), `::an_identical_monitor_keeps_its_id_while_it_is_there` (every on/off transition of the two, an unplug and a replug on another port, a new monitor beside one off), and `crates/strand-surface/src/monitor.rs::tests::identical_monitors_take_the_outputs_numbers` (the swap with the old `wl_output` removed first and last, both off and on in the other order, a monitor the list does not yet name, no list).

**2026-11-07 · output-id review round 4: the ids are given out only while a run of `outputs` is up, a new run's heads take the ids shown, and the connector is taken out of every form a compositor writes it in.** The process-wide list of connector and `Output.id` (`strand_services::outputs::ids()`) was written only by a run's snapshots and kept when the run ended, so with `outputs` stopped (nobody reading it, 5 s after its last reader, a reload, a failure backing off) a monitor moved to another port met its own old entry on the connector it had left, and `Monitors::number` gave it ` #2`, against the documented fallback to plug order; the next run then numbered the head on the new port afresh, so `Output.id` and `Screen.id` disagreed. Now the list says whether a run is up (`Ids::live`, set at each shared snapshot, cleared when a run ends and when its manager goes), and `ids()` is empty while none is, so `Screen.id` falls back to plug order then. The other direction is fixed too: the binary's host tells strand-services each monitor it shows (`strand_services::outputs::shown`, from `monitor_added` and `monitor_removed`), and a run's heads new to it take those ids first and the last run's only for connectors not shown (a monitor off), so a run started after anything that happened while none was up agrees with `Screen.id` for every monitor shown (two identical monitors swapped between ports while no run was up gave the old run's numbers to the wrong ones). Clearing the list when a run ends was not taken: a monitor off has no `wl_output`, and only the last run's list keeps its number. Separately, `identity_description` and its copy `output_id` removed only an exact trailing ` (<connector>)`; wlroots writes ` (<connector> via <subconnector>)` when a DP connector drives an HDMI or DVI sink, and smithay (niri) builds a description as `make - model - connector` (its nested `wl_output` says `Smithay - Winit - winit`, seen in the matrix image), so the id kept the port there. Both now also take off ` (<c> via …)` and a trailing ` - <c>`. Tests, each failing without its fix: `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::ids_are_given_only_while_a_run_is_up`, `crates/strand-surface/src/monitor.rs::tests::connector_suffix_is_not_identity` and `crates/strand/src/services/mod.rs::output_id::an_outputs_id_is_its_screens_id` (the `via` and niri forms, and one monitor on two ports).

## settings-tables

**2026-11-07 · settings-tables: settings files read TOML's table forms and keep them; a list is merged by value.** A record or a list of records in a settings file read only as inline values, so `[profiles.desk]` and `[[pins]]` failed with "expected Profile"; any shell write of such a field replaced a `[section]` the user wrote with one inline line and dropped its comments (`merge_item` had no case for a record over a section or a list over an array of tables), and an unknown key in a record was ignored, so `enabeld = false` read as the default. Now `persist::decode_item` reads a `Table` wherever a record goes and an `ArrayOfTables` wherever a list of records goes, recursively, so `profiles: [text: Profile]` reads `[profiles.desk]` with `[[profiles.desk.mons]]`. A key the record does not have is the existing per-field bad value that keeps the last good value (spec 11), its message naming where it is (`profiles: "desk": mons[0]: unknown field "scael"`); this goes against the fewest-concepts reading on purpose, because settings apply live and a silently ignored typo in a display profile is a hazard, and it adds no concept. Write-back (`settings.rs`) leaves a value that reads the same as the new one as written (`same_item`: `1` is `1.0`, a section equals the inline table of its keys, key order ignored), keeps a record over a `[section]` a section merged key by key, writes a new record among section-written siblings as a section shaped like them, and merges arrays, inline or of tables, by value: a new element takes the first unused old one that reads the same, else the first whose every key it has with the same value (an element that left fields to their defaults), keeping its text and comments in the new order; any other is written afresh, and an unmatched old one is removed. Merging by position was rejected: an insert in the middle would attach one element's comments to another. The cost is that an element that changes is written afresh without the comments on it; a comment that must survive edits goes above the record's own section, which is merged key by key. An empty list is written `name = []`, since no `[[name]]` at all would read as the default. Tables print in the order of their place in the file, so a reordered array of tables moves the tables it moves (and those under them) to the place of the last one before them (`keep_order`). In an array spread over lines, the comment after an element's comma (which toml_edit files with the next element) stays with its element. TOML 1.1's inline tables over several lines parse under toml_edit 0.25.15 (`records_read_from_sections_and_arrays_of_tables`). spec 10.3 is corrected: it said a persist store edited by hand is read, but the store's checksum makes such a store corrupt (moved aside, the default and a warning); the behaviour stays, and values people edit belong in a settings file. A `key` clause on settings list fields is deferred: a dictionary keyed by name covers profiles, pins and rules. Tests: `crates/strand-compiler/src/vm/persist.rs::tests::records_read_from_sections_and_arrays_of_tables`, `crates/strand-core/tests/settings.rs::a_write_to_one_record_leaves_the_others_as_written`, `::an_array_of_tables_is_merged_by_value`, `::a_multi_line_array_keeps_its_layout`, `::a_record_section_stays_a_section`, `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::settings_records_read_and_write_table_forms`.

**2026-11-07 · settings-tables review round 1: a field whose value in the file is bad is not written.** An unknown key failing the whole field, together with write-back writing a field while it is in error and a dictionary's merge deleting the keys the new value lacks, meant one typo (or a record field removed from the `type`) plus a "Save this profile" deleted every other profile from a hand-kept file. Each field now remembers whether the file's value for it read (`Field::bad`); a write of a bad field is kept live and not saved, with a `WriteFailed` notice naming the field ("not saved while its value in the file is bad; fix it there"), and once the file reads again its value wins. This follows what a file with a syntax error already got (never overwritten). Scoping the error to the bad entry, keeping the good profiles, was not taken: it would make a dictionary's errors different from every other field's, and a write would still drop the bad entry's text. A write to the overlay (a read-only file, a runtime overlay value) is not held. Test: `crates/strand-core/tests/settings.rs::a_field_whose_file_value_is_bad_is_not_overwritten`.

**2026-11-08 · settings-tables follow-up: a write keeps every comment it did not change; a changed element keeps its own.** The first rule wrote an element of a list that changed afresh, so re-saving one monitor of a `[[profiles.desk.mons]]` list dropped the comments on it, and, because toml_edit files the text above a table header (the file's header comment included) with that table, a changed or removed first table took the file's header with it. Users keep these files by hand (the owner's monitors.toml is in chezmoi), so the rule is now what a careful hand edit would leave. Every comment and blank line outside what changed stays. A changed element keeps its comments, keys and key order, only the changed values replaced, each keeping its decor (spacing and the comment after it). A new element is written in the shape of its siblings (sections where they are sections, `[[…]]` where they have them, their key order), and a removed element's own comments go with it. Which old element a new one is matched with now runs in four rounds, each over what the earlier ones left: one that reads the same; a record whose every key the new one has with the same value (a field left to its default); a record most of whose keys' values the new one has (`2 × shared > keys`, the most shared first: a field or two changed); and, for a run of new elements left between the same two kept neighbours, the old ones left between them, in order, the pairs that share the most values first (`in_order`, a weighted in-order matching: an element changed in place, including a one-key pin renamed and a scalar in a multi-line array, and not an element added beside it). Rounds of matching cost at most the old length times the new, plus a sort of the candidate pairs, so a long list of scalars stays cheap. The objection to position, that an insert in the middle would attach one element's comments to another, does not apply to the last round, since an insert takes an old element only where one was removed in that same gap. The text above a table or key is split at its last blank line (`split_lead`): the comment lines right above it are its own and go where it goes; what is above that blank line (a header, a commented-out block) is the file's. In an array of tables the file's parts are places that stay where they are, the k-th table printed taking the k-th, so a reorder moves each element with its own comments and leaves the header at the top; a removed table's place goes unless a new table takes it, and comments in a place that goes, or above a removed section, dictionary entry or key, are put above what follows it (the next key of its table, else the first table printed after it, else the file's end: `Orphans`). A comment written right above a table with no blank line between is that table's, so a header comment needs a blank line under it to stay when the first table goes; this follows how people separate a header and costs nothing for one that is. Diffing the old and new text line by line was not taken: it would match by text, not by what the values mean, and lose the "reads the same" rule (`1` for `1.0`, keys in another order). Tests: `crates/strand-core/tests/settings.rs::a_write_keeps_every_comment_it_did_not_change` (one field of one element, an element added in its siblings' key order, the first removed, a reorder, a key removed from a section under a note), `::a_header_above_the_first_table_stays` (a two-key element changed in one field, replaced in place, and changed with a new one added before it, the first table removed, a dictionary entry removed), `::a_multi_line_array_keeps_its_layout` (a scalar changed in place keeps the comment on its line), `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::settings_records_read_and_write_table_forms` (the saved profile's changed monitor keeps `# the big one` and `# left`).

## monitor-layout

**2026-11-07 · monitor-layout: a best-guess monitor layout is written with the list operations there are; no `scan` or running total was added.** The owner wants a set of monitors no saved profile matches to get a best guess, left to right as hyprpier's Detect does, so the question was whether a config can say "each output's x is the sum of the logical widths before it" today. It can: `order.take(order.index_of(p => p.name == o.name) ?? 0).sum(p => wide(p))`, where `sort_by(o => o.name.starts_with("eDP"))` puts the laptop's panel last (a stable sort, `false` before `true`), `wide` matches `OutputTransform` to take the mode's height for a turned head and divides by `scale` with `.round()`, and every value fits `OutputChange`, so `outputs.apply(guess)` type-checks. The cost is quadratic in the number of outputs, which is at most a handful. `sum` and `reduce` already existed (spec 7.1, functions.md), so under "does it remove a concept, or add one?" nothing was added: an indexed `map` would give every chain operation a second lambda arity (lowering treats them as incremental with one argument), and a `scan` would be a second fold beside `reduce`. A single-pass `reduce` into a list of changes was not documented, because it depends on how an empty list literal is typed as `init`, which no test pins. site/how-to/monitor-profiles.md shows the best guess and saved layouts, one per set of monitors keyed by their `Output.id`s, in a settings file that uses settings-tables' sections, applied at start through `outputs.ready` and written to the compositor's file through a live `text:` (decisions.md monitor-profiles). Test: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_best_guess_layout_is_written_with_the_list_operations_there_are`, and the page's own configs through strand-site's build test.

## dbus-unfollowed

**2026-11-07 · dbus-unfollowed: a `from dbus` field bound to a property that never signals is a warning; the lid is a recipe.** strand-introspect dropped annotations, so a field bound to a property annotated `org.freedesktop.DBus.Property.EmitsChangedSignal=false` (logind's `Docked` and `OnExternalPower`) read once and then went stale with no word. `strand_introspect::Property` now carries `emits: Emits` (`True`, `Invalidates`, `Const`, `False`), read from the annotation inside the `<property>`, else the one written directly inside its `<interface>` (logind writes it after the properties, so the interface's default is applied when the interface closes), else `True` as the specification says; an annotation inside a method or signal is theirs. The compiler cannot depend on strand-introspect (zbus; it is built for wasm), so `check::dbus::BusProperty` carries its own copy, `check::dbus::Emits`, converted by crates/strand's `bus_emits` and strand-dev's workspace, and gained `Default` so the tests' literals stay short. `check::dbus_unfollowed` is a warning (a config is not broken by a daemon's property), naming the field and pointing at an event-driven source or `from poll`; `const` and `invalidates` are silent, the runtime already reading an invalidated property again. A daemon that leaves the annotation out of a property that never signals is not caught. dbusmock's introspection carries no annotations, so the warning is tested from XML: strand-introspect's parse, the checker with fakes, and crates/strand's loader over a parsed XML. The lid gets no builtin field: UPower's `LidIsClosed`, `LidIsPresent` and `OnBattery` signal their changes, and a `from dbus` service follows them today, which the guide (level 5) and site/how-to/dbus-and-actions.md show and a dbusmock test pins. A `lid_closed` on `battery` would misname the lid, and one on `session` would add a subscription path to a method-driven service. `docked` is offered nowhere: logind never signals it, and the set of monitors in `outputs.all` is the event-driven truth. Tests: `crates/strand-introspect/src/lib.rs::tests::emits_changed_signal_is_read_from_the_property_or_its_interface`, `crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::a_property_that_never_signals_is_warned_about`, `crates/strand/src/services/custom.rs::tests::a_never_signalled_property_from_introspection_is_warned_about`, `crates/strand-services/tests/custom.rs::the_lid_recipe_follows_upower`.

## dbus-sets-parked

**2026-11-07 · dbus-sets-parked: sets of D-Bus objects stay builtin-only.** A `from dbus` service reads one object at one path, so following a daemon's set of objects (boltd's devices, ModemManager's modems, logind's sessions) has no config spelling. Every such daemon on the owner's machine (BlueZ, iwd, UDisks2, UPower) is already a builtin, and the case that raised it, approving Thunderbolt devices through bolt, is parked by the owner, who wants Strand's capabilities over a Strand panel for it; the security fix is outside Strand anyway (install bolt, enrol the dock, then drop the udev rule that authorises every device). The routes today: a fixed-path `from dbus` service for a known device with `action authorize(flags: text) = Authorize`, the manager's `EnrollDevice` as an action, and `boltctl monitor` through `from listen`. For a revival: the shape is `service x from dbus system "bus" "/path/*" key field { … }`, listing an ObjectManager where one exists, else child nodes listed again on the owner's signals under that path only; method results and signal events (what fwupd needs) are a separate block; and reading an object that appears later must match only an ObjectManager or the parent path, never every signal of a daemon, or an idle shell would wake on unrelated signals.

## ws-move

**2026-11-07 · ws-move: `ws.move_to(screen)`; ext-workspace `assign` deferred.** A workspace could only be focused, so placing one on a screen took a declared action per compositor (string-built Lua on Hyprland), and a declared action without a result keeps only its latest queued call, so a loop of moves lost the middle ones. `Workspace` gains `action move_to(screen: Screen)`, mirroring `win.move_to(ws)`: the argument is a `Screen`, since only a screen that is on takes a workspace. It is `WmAction::MoveWorkspace { workspace, screen }` on the adapters: Hyprland's Lua `hl.dsp.workspace.move({ workspace = …, monitor = … })` first and the classic `moveworkspacetomonitor` on a hyprlang Hyprland, as the other dispatches go; sway's `move workspace to output`, picked by a window on the workspace (`[con_id=…]`), else the focused workspace, else (an empty workspace shown on another output) switched to first, with the focus switched back in the same command because sway's move focuses the moved workspace; niri's `MoveWorkspaceToMonitor` by id. Each adapter answers a workspace already on that screen `Ok` without a request, so a placement is idempotent; a workspace not made yet is `UnknownWorkspace` (the compositor's own rules place it when it is made), and a screen that is not on is a new `WmError::UnknownScreen`, which sway checks against a `get_outputs` read at the move and Hyprland and niri against their state. Each call is its own request, so a `for` of moves sends every one. Pinned on real compositors (`compositor_matrix.rs::a_workspace_is_moved_to_another_screen`, sway in the matrix, Hyprland 0.57 nested by scripts/container/hyprland-nested.sh, and `tests/sway.rs::sway_moves_a_workspace_to_another_output`): the focus stays on the workspace that had it, so moving the focused one takes the focus along; a screen left with no workspace gets a new empty one of the compositor's; on sway the moved workspace is shown on its new screen (an empty one shown there before is let go, as sway lets go of every empty workspace it does not show, and an empty workspace moved off focus is let go the same way), while on Hyprland a hidden workspace stays hidden there. niri's matrix has one output (nested on winit), so its leg checks that niri takes the request as the adapter writes it and that a move to the workspace's own output is `Ok`; its move across outputs is unit-tested only. ext-workspace-v1's `assign` is deferred: every compositor that offers it has an adapter, and the CI image's sway 1.9 cannot test it; revisit at sway 1.12 or for a compositor without an adapter. No service-level `workspaces.move`.

**2026-11-07 · ws-move review round 1: the classic dispatcher refuses a workspace name with a space.** Hyprland's classic `moveworkspacetomonitor` splits its argument at the first space, and on 0.56 a named workspace is addressed by `name:<name>`, so `my web` read as `name:my` on monitor `web DP-1`. The classic form now fails with `Unsupported` for a target with a space instead of moving another workspace; the Lua dispatcher (0.57) takes the name as one string. Test: `crates/strand-services/src/wm/hyprland.rs::tests::a_workspace_is_moved_to_a_monitor`.

**2026-11-07 · ws-move review round 2: sway refuses an empty workspace moved behind the focused one.** sway keeps an empty workspace only while it is shown. Moving one that another screen shows, onto the screen that shows the focused workspace, switched to it, moved it and switched back, which hid it there, so sway removed it (and made a fresh one on the screen it left) while the call answered Ok. That move now fails with `Unsupported` (`sway.rs::tests::a_workspace_is_moved_to_an_output`); onto any other screen it still moves, the moved workspace shown there and the focus back where it was. Chosen over skipping the switch back, which would break the promise that the focus stays on the workspace that had it; an empty workspace has no windows to carry, and the compositor's own rules place it when it is made.

## action-coalesced

**2026-11-07 · action-coalesced: a declared action without a result called together is a warning.** spec.md 5.7 runs an action without `-> T` at most once at a time, a call while it runs replacing the queued one, so `for ws in workspaces.all { place(ws.name) }` sent the first and the last and dropped the rest without a word. `check::action_coalesced` warns at a call of such an action in a `for` body of a handler, and at a call after another call of the same action that runs first on every path of the handler: one in the same block or an enclosing one, earlier (the checker keeps the actions called per block, so calls on exclusive branches of an `if` or a `match` are silent, and a call after an `if` that held one is not counted). The help offers both ways out, one call for all items or a `-> text` action awaited each time, and says that when only the latest call matters the code is right; it is a warning, not an error, for that case. Two calls in a row lose nothing when the action was idle, but lose the first when it still runs from before, so the second call is warned about too. Builtin service actions (`ws.move_to`, `p.select()`) are exempt: each is its own request. Test: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/checker.rs::an_action_without_a_result_called_together_is_warned_about`.

## json-fn

**2026-11-07 · json-fn: `json(value)` writes plain data as compact JSON.** A config that wrote a JSON file for a tool, passed a record to a declared action as one argument, or copied structured data had to build the text by hand with `join` and its own escaping. `json(v)` is a pure builtin over `any?`: a record is an object of its fields in declaration order, a list an array, a dictionary an object of its keys' texts in key order (an `int` key `"3"`: JSON's keys are texts), null `null`, an enum its variant's name, a colour `"#rrggbb"` (`"#rrggbbaa"` when translucent, where `hex` without `alpha: true` is an error), a duration its milliseconds, a whole number whole (`2`, not `2.0`: JSON has one kind of number) and any other in its shortest form (non-finite: `null`); texts are escaped as JSON requires and keep their other characters; what is not data (a function, an element) is `null`. It is not a universal quoter: a control character comes out as `\u001b`, which Lua reads otherwise, so Lua (and anything not JSON) takes a `fn` of its own. The persist store's encoder was not reused: it is driven by the declared type and writes a dictionary as pairs, where a file for a tool wants an object. Test: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/flex.rs::json_writes_plain_data`.

**2026-11-07 · json-fn review round 3: `json` writes a token as its value.** `$fg` is a `Value::Token` in the VM, and a record or dictionary built from it keeps the token, which `json` had no arm for and wrote as `null`: `json(Colors(fg: $fg, bg: $surface))` in a `file` text (always a VM chunk, `json` being no template function) wrote `{"fg":null,"bg":null}`, the hole round 2 closed for `join`. A token now reads through `VmHooks::token` over the current table, as `join` and `hex` do, and is written as its value would be: a colour `"#rrggbb"` (`"#rrggbbaa"` translucent), a number, length or angle a number in its shortest form, a duration its milliseconds, a text or keyword a string; a token with no value, or one JSON has no form for (a font, a shadow), is `json`'s error, never `null`. Test: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::json_writes_a_token_as_its_value` (colour tokens in a record's fields and a dictionary's value, a length token, following a theme flip), failing without the fix with every token `null`.

## outputs-resync

**2026-11-07 · outputs-resync: a change the output manager sends with no `done` has the manager bound again.** Run on nested Hyprland 0.57, `outputs.all` went stale after the first change of the session: a move made with `hyprctl eval 'hl.monitor(…)'` or Strand's own `outputs.apply` comes as head events carrying the values from before the change (NESTED-2's `position(1280, 0)` after a move to 2000), and no manager `done`, while xdg-output says the new place and a client bound afterwards gets the outputs as they are. The service published only at `done`, so the page's `monitors.lua` and "Save this profile" recorded a layout that no longer held. Under fix-in-Strand, the service now notes a head or mode event that comes after a `done` (`Client::touched`), and when no `done` follows within 250 ms (`RESYNC_AFTER`) and no configuration is in flight, it binds the manager again and stops the old one (`Client::resync`): what was published stands until the new manager's first `done`, each head keeps its id (`Client::carried`), and `ready` stays true. wlroots, niri and labwc send the `done` with the change, so they never resync. Hyprland never answers `stop` with `finished` and goes on sending the stopped manager its changes, so a manager that is not the current one is ignored (its new heads released) and nothing is kept of it. Reading positions from xdg-output instead was not taken: the head's mode and scale lag too, and a resync takes every field from the one source. Checked on nested Hyprland 0.57 (`scripts/container/hyprland-nested.sh`): after the `hyprctl` move `outputs.all` showed NESTED-1 at 2960 and NESTED-2 at 2000, as `hyprctl -j monitors` did, and after an `outputs.apply` to x 3000 the same. Test, failing without the fix (it waits 10 s for the move): `crates/strand-services/tests/outputs.rs::a_change_with_no_done_is_read_again`, against strand-fake-wayland's new output management in Hyprland's shape (`OutputManagement::Lagging`) and wlroots'; and `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::a_change_with_no_done_is_resynced`.

**2026-11-07 · outputs-resync review round 4: the heads are checked against xdg-output, since Hyprland often sends the manager nothing.** The round-4 check found the resync too narrow on nested Hyprland 0.57: a move made the way the page's `monitors.lua` writes it (`hl.monitor({ …, mode, position, scale })`) sends the manager no event at all, so nothing started a resync, and after one resync the next change went only to the stopped manager (a `done` per monitor) and nothing to the one bound after it, so only the first change of a session was followed. Hyprland's source says why: a head is updated only on the monitor's `modeChanged` (with the values it had then), the `done` comes only with a new head or a monitor going, and a stopped manager whose heads were released is still sent `ensureMonitorSent`'s `done`; the manager is right only at bind. Its `wl_output` and xdg-output follow every change, xdg-output's place and size on every layout change, each batch ended by the `wl_output`'s `done`. So the service now binds xdg-output and, once a `wl_output` has been quiet for 250 ms after a `done` that follows the manager's first, checks the heads on against it (`Client::disagrees`: place, mode size and rate within 0.5 Hz, transform, and the logical size against the mode over the scale within 2 px) and binds the manager again when they disagree; the 250 ms rule for a change with no `done` stays. One check per batch, so a compositor that rounds differently costs a resync per change, never a loop. The source of every field is still the manager bound last; xdg-output only says that it is stale. Each resync leaves Hyprland one stopped manager on the connection (`stop` is never answered), sent a `done` per monitor at each config reload, which is small next to how rarely monitors change; reconnecting would free it and was not taken, since a rebind carries the ids and keeps the run ready with less. Checked on nested Hyprland 0.57: six full `hl.monitor` moves, four position-only ones, a scale change and a hotplug were each followed in `outputs.all` as `hyprctl -j monitors` showed them (12 resyncs); on headless sway a move, two scales, a rotation, a mode, and turning a head off and on made no resync. Tests, failing without the fix: `crates/strand-services/tests/outputs.rs::a_change_with_no_done_is_read_again` (four moves; the fake gains Hyprland's `OutputManagement::Silent` shape, its xdg-output, and stopped managers sent `done`s), `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::heads_behind_their_outputs_are_resynced`.

## outputs-apply

**2026-11-08 · outputs-apply: the outputs are read again on a connection of their own, and every configuration is made on the one manager the service binds.** On nested Hyprland 0.57, after `hyprctl output create headless HOT-1`, the monitor-profiles page's guess (NESTED-1 x 1920, NESTED-2 x 3840, HOT-1 x 0) was answered `succeeded` and `hyprctl -j monitors` showed nothing moved; the apply at start had worked. Reproduced with a throwaway config and `WAYLAND_DEBUG=client`: an apply of NESTED-2 to x 3000 on manager #4 took, the service then resynced (its own apply is a change Hyprland sends with no `done`), stopping #4 and binding #12, and the next apply, on #12, moved only HOT-1, leaving NESTED-1 and NESTED-2 where #4's apply had put them. With no first apply, the same guess on the first manager took in full. Hyprland's source says why (`src/protocols/OutputManagement.cpp`, `src/config/shared/monitor/MonitorRuleManager.cpp`): `apply` saves each head's state in the manager the configuration was made on (`m_owner->m_monitorStates`) and schedules a rule reload, which answers `succeeded` once done whatever it did; the reload takes each monitor's rule from `getOutputStateFor`, the first manager in `m_managers`, all clients' in the order they were bound, that saved a state for it; and a manager leaves that list only when its resource is destroyed, which `stop` never does (Hyprland sends no `finished`, and the protocol has no destructor), so only the client disconnecting ends it. Each resync's stopped manager therefore stayed for the run (follow-up 2) and kept its saved states above every later configuration (follow-up 3). Under fix-in-Strand the service no longer binds a second manager on its connection: a resync reads the outputs on a short connection of its own that binds the manager alone, reads to its first `done` (2 s at most, `READ_WAIT`) and closes, which ends that manager with it (`read_again`), and takes what it read into the heads of the same name (`Client::take_fresh`: each keeps its proxy, its listed modes and its id; a current mode not among them is `HeadEntry::shown_mode`). The manager bound at start is never stopped, so on Hyprland the connection holds one manager for the run, and every configuration is made on it, the oldest Strand has, whose saved states each apply updates. A configuration asked for while the heads may be behind (a change with no `done` yet, or `wl_output`s that moved and disagree) is made after a read, so it does not move back what the unread change moved. wlroots, niri and labwc never read again. Reconnecting the whole service when stopped managers piled up was not taken: it would drop the saved states of every configuration applied, which Hyprland would then revert at its next rule reload. Still Hyprland's and out of Strand's hands: a monitor Strand has configured follows Strand's saved state above Hyprland's own monitor rules while the shell runs (a `hyprctl eval 'hl.monitor(…)'` move of it is overridden at the reload it triggers), as for any output-management client that stays connected, and another client's manager bound earlier that configured a monitor wins over Strand's, which the check below reports. Checked on nested Hyprland 0.57: the hotplug-then-apply run moved all three (NESTED-1 1280, NESTED-2 2560, HOT-1 0) with no `stop` sent; six `hl.monitor` moves, three applies, a hotplug and its removal, and four more moves left 9 manager binds (the start's and one per read), no `stop`, and the process's sockets at 7 before and after, `outputs.all` as `hyprctl -j monitors` said at each step; on headless sway each run opened one connection and bound one manager. Tests, failing without the fix: `crates/strand-services/tests/outputs.rs::every_apply_is_followed_after_a_resync` (the fake's Hyprland shapes now save a configuration in its manager and follow the oldest connected one, `getOutputStateFor`'s rule), `::stopped_managers_do_not_pile_up` (`Fake::output_managers`), `::an_apply_right_after_a_change_keeps_it`, and `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::a_read_again_is_taken_into_the_heads`.

**2026-11-08 · outputs-apply: an applied configuration is `succeeded` once the outputs show it, else `failed` saying how they differ.** Hyprland answers `succeeded` after its rule reload whatever the reload did, so `succeeded` alone could claim a layout the compositor did not take (the case above, and still the case when another client's earlier manager configured a monitor). `outputs.succeeded("apply")` now waits until the `wl_output`s and xdg-outputs show what the configuration asked (`Client::unlike`): a head asked off has no `wl_output`, a head asked on has one with its mode in, and with xdg-output its place and size in, that agrees in place, mode size and rate (within 0.5 Hz; a rate of 0 is not compared), transform, and logical size against the mode over the scale (within 2 px), the same comparison the resync check makes (`differs`). When they still differ once they have been quiet for 1 s after the answer (`CHECK_QUIET`; 5 s at most while they keep changing, `CHECK_FOR`), the apply is `outputs.failed("apply", "the compositor said it applied the configuration, but NESTED-2 is at 3000, 0, not 2560, 0")`. The wait starts at the compositor's answer, so it measures nothing on a slow machine: wlroots' changes come before its `succeeded` and agree at once, and Hyprland answers only after its reload, which waits for a frame (3.5 s on nested Hyprland's idle headless outputs, until a hotplug drew one). Adaptive sync is not checked, as no `wl_output` says it; a compositor whose `wl_output`s carry no names (before version 4) is taken at its word, and `test` stays `succeeded` at its answer, as it changes nothing. The configuration being checked holds the queue, as one in flight does, and is `failed` with the rest if the connection goes. Tests, failing without it: `crates/strand-services/tests/outputs.rs::an_apply_the_compositor_did_not_take_fails` (`Cmd::ShadowOutput`, another client's earlier manager), `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::an_applied_configuration_is_checked_against_the_outputs`, `::a_check_waits_for_the_outputs_to_be_quiet`; the sway tests (`outputs_lists_configures_and_tests_sways_heads`) pass unchanged.

**2026-11-08 · outputs-apply review round 5: the check takes a scale as it was sent and as the compositor rounds it, a mirror's missing `wl_output` tells nothing, and `succeeded` comes after `outputs.all` shows the apply.** Three findings on the check above, each confirmed against the code and Hyprland 0.57's source. (1) A scale is sent as a `wl_fixed`, which wayland-client truncates to 1/256 (wayland-scanner's `(s * 256.) as i32`), and the check compared the logical size with the mode over the scale asked: sway takes 1.33 as 340/256 and lays a 3840-wide monitor out 2891 wide, 3.8 px from 3840/1.33, past the 2 px slack, so an apply sway carried out was `failed`. Hyprland goes further: `CMonitor::applyMonitorRule` takes a scale whose logical size is not whole to the nearest one on a 1/120 grid that gives whole pixels, so 4/3, which Hyprland sends as 341/256 and a profile saved from `outputs.all` asks, is 1.3333 and 2880 wide, 2.8 px from 3840/(341/256): every apply of a saved 4/3 profile was `failed`, and the resync check found such a head disagreeing with its xdg-output after every change. `Expect.scale` is now the scale as sent (`sent_scale`), and a logical size agrees when it is within 2 px or when the scale it shows (mode over logical size) is within 1/128 of it (`SCALE_SLACK`: two `wl_fixed` steps, the client's truncation and the compositor's rounding), in `differs`, so the resync check takes it too; a scale moved further (Hyprland's 1.5 on 1440 lines is 1.6) is still `failed`, its error showing the scale to two decimals. (2) Hyprland removes a mirrored monitor's `wl_output` (`CProtocolManager::onMonitorModeChange`) and sends its head as on, so a configuration includes it on and the check said "HDMI-A-1 is not on" for every apply with a mirror. A head on with no `wl_output` when the configuration is made is now `Expect.unseen`, and having none tells nothing of it; it is compared once it has one, and a head turned on from off must still get one. (3) Hyprland's reload sends the heads their old values (or nothing) while the `wl_output`s move, so the check could pass while `outputs.all`, built from the heads, still showed the layout before the apply until the resync 250 ms later, and a handler on `succeeded` that saved `outputs.all` saved the old layout. When the check passes while the heads may be behind (`Client::stale`), the outputs are read again and published before `succeeded` is emitted. Also fixed: `Fake::sync` answered before the fake flushed what the commands sent, so a client woken after it could act before their events reached it (`an_apply_right_after_a_change_keeps_it` failed once in a loaded run); it now answers after the flush. The monitor-profiles page says that on Hyprland a monitor Strand arranged does not move by hand while the shell runs, so its section in the file is what to edit. Checked on nested Hyprland 0.57: two applies, NESTED-1 at scale 1.33 (Hyprland showed 1.3333334, the apply `succeeded`), a move after it, then HOT-1 plugged in and mirrored onto NESTED-1 (its `wl_output` removed) and two applies with it, each `succeeded`, with `outputs.all` read in the `succeeded` handler showing the places Hyprland then reported. Tests, failing without the fixes: `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::a_fractional_scale_is_checked_as_it_was_sent_and_rounded`, `::a_plan_is_checked_as_it_was_sent`, `::an_applied_configuration_is_checked_against_the_outputs` (its mirror case), `crates/strand-services/tests/outputs.rs::an_apply_with_a_mirror_is_checked_on_the_others` (`FakeBuilder::mirrors`), `::succeeded_comes_after_outputs_all_shows_the_apply`.

**2026-11-08 · outputs-apply review round 6: a mirror is checked by its head for what an apply changed of it, a mirror not named is sent no mode, and the scale as sent has a case of its own.** Three findings on round 5, each reproduced first. (1) A head on with no `wl_output` (`Expect.unseen`, a Hyprland mirror) told nothing, so on nested Hyprland 0.57 `outputs.apply([OutputChange(name: "HOT-1", x: 5000, y: 0)])` for HOT-1 mirrored onto NESTED-1 was `succeeded` while `hyprctl` and the heads still put it at 0, 200: Hyprland saves the place in the manager's state, its rule reload keeps the rule's mirror, and it answers `succeeded`. `Expect.unseen` now carries the head's place, transform and scale when the configuration was made (`Was`), and until it has a `wl_output` each of those the configuration changed must be the head's now (its scale within `SCALE_SLACK`), else the apply is `failed` ("HOT-1, a mirror with no wl_output, is at 0, 0, not 5000, 0"; `Client::unseen_unlike`). What it left as it was is not compared, as a mirror's head can move with the monitor it mirrors, so an apply naming other monitors, or a profile saved from `outputs.all`, still passes. The head is not read again at the check's deadline: a mirror's head that is behind is already read again before the configuration is made (`Client::stale`), and no compositor known takes a mirror's place without saying so. (2) An apply naming other monitors changed a mirror's mode: Hyprland's mirror head names no current mode and has no `wl_output`, so `default_mode` fell back to the preferred mode and sent `set_mode` (nested: HOT-1 at 1280x720 went to 1920x1080 on an apply of NESTED-2 alone). A head already on that shows no mode Strand can name is now sent no mode, which Hyprland (`applyTestConfiguration` saves a mode only when one is set) and wlroots (a configuration head starts from the head's state) both keep; a head turned on from off still gets its preferred, else its first. `OutputChange.mode`'s doc says what null does. (3) `sent_scale` was proved only by asserts on its own value, as `SCALE_SLACK` covers what truncation does for a compositor that lays the scale it was sent out to whole pixels. It matters when the compositor's rounding moves the scale up to two steps from the one sent, the other way from the truncation: 1.26 is sent as 322/256 (1.2578), and 3840x2160 laid out 3069x1726 (1.2512) is within 1/128 of that but 0.0088 from 1.26. That case is now in the test, and fails with `sent_scale` the identity. The fake's mirrors name no current mode, and in Hyprland's shapes stay where they are when a configuration places them. Checked on nested Hyprland 0.57 with HOT-1 hotplugged and mirrored onto NESTED-1 by `hl.monitor`: an apply of NESTED-2 alone `succeeded` with HOT-1's head enabled and sent no mode, and HOT-1 stayed 1280x720 through six applies; HOT-1 at 5000, 0 was `failed` with the error above; HOT-1 at its own place, NESTED-2 back, NESTED-1 at 1.33 (Hyprland 1.3333334) and back each `succeeded` with `outputs.all` as `hyprctl` said; no `stop`, sockets 7. Still open, from round 5: a profile saved with a mirror keeps its null mode as 0x0, which `placed` sends and the service refuses. Tests, failing without the fixes: `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::a_mirror_is_checked_by_its_head_for_what_was_changed`, `crates/strand-services/tests/outputs.rs::an_apply_placing_a_mirror_that_stays_fails` (1), `crates/strand-services/src/outputs.rs::tests::a_mirror_keeps_its_mode_when_another_head_changes` (2), `::a_fractional_scale_is_checked_as_it_was_sent_and_rounded` (its 1.26 case, 3).

**2026-11-08 · outputs-apply: the compositor matrix checks `outputs` on every compositor, and a profile places a monitor saved with no mode with none.** Nothing in `compositor_matrix.rs` used the `outputs` service, so GitHub's compositors job, the only place a real Hyprland runs on a KMS card, never checked the fixes above. `the_outputs_service_follows_the_live_compositor` runs `strand run` with a probe shell (its `outputs.all` and `screens.all` read back with `strand get --json`) wherever `zwlr_output_manager_v1` is offered: `outputs.all` must list what `swaymsg -t get_outputs`, `hyprctl -j monitors all` and `niri msg outputs` list (on or off, place, the mode's size), and on labwc, with no IPC, agree with the `screens` the same process has from the `wl_output`s and xdg-outputs; every output on must have its screen's `id`; a move from outside before any apply (`swaymsg output … position`, Hyprland's monitor rule by `keyword`, else `eval` of `hl.monitor`, `niri msg output … position set`) must be followed; and with a second output an apply 500 px right and back must be `succeeded` with `outputs.all` already showing it, the compositor showing it and the ids kept. The move from outside comes before the apply because Hyprland follows the oldest manager that configured a monitor. A Hyprland rule reloads every monitor, and one placed `auto` by the config's rule moved (nested, NESTED-1 went to 3060 when NESTED-2 was ruled to 1780), so every monitor on is pinned where it is first and the test checks that the others stay. With the 250 ms resync off (`RESYNC_AFTER` an hour), the test fails on nested Hyprland 0.57 at the move from outside (`outputs.all` keeps NESTED-2 at 1280); it passes on sway, niri and labwc in `matrix.sh` and on nested Hyprland. Round 6's open item: the page's `placed` sends `mode: null` when the saved width is 0 (a mirror's), which keeps the monitor's mode, where it sent `OutputMode(0, 0, 0)`, which the service refuses, failing the whole profile (`crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::the_monitor_profiles_page_places_a_monitor_saved_with_no_mode_with_none`, failing without it).

## handler-fault

**2026-11-08 · handler-fault: a handler's error is a value and freezes nothing; spec.md 8.3 and 12 say so (section 14).** A builder's panel had a button whose `on click` awaited an action that failed (`["false"]`, exit 1; or `echo abc` read as `-> int`), and after that click no other button of the panel ran its handler. The cause was not the `await` path: the coroutine ended with its error as it should, the VM's `reporting` wrapper located it, and the shell's `after_step` called `Instance::freeze` on every runtime error of the tick, a handler's included, which suspended the panel's instance (input dropped) and outlined it red. The docs disagreed with one another: spec.md 8.3 says "a handler's errors are values: a failing action or expression never stops other handlers or the shell", design.md says handlers "return errors as values", while spec.md 12's "runtime faults freeze only their own component" and the site's troubleshooting page ("such as a handler that fails") were read to cover them. The reading that removes a concept is 8.3's: a handler's error ends that run only, as its own value, and is reported (the log, a `strand watch` `fault` with `frozen: false`) without taking the component's other handlers, its timers or its bindings down with it; a binding's fault, whose value the screen cannot show, still freezes its component. Freezing for a handler also hid a hazard: one failing `await` made every button of a panel dead until a reload. `RuntimeError` gains `handler` (set by `reporting`, the wrapper every `on`, `after` and `every` body runs in), and `Instance::freeze` returns false for it, outlining nothing. In the `lock`, a handler's error still takes its instance's nodes to the built-in password field (`lock_faults` is unchanged): a lock whose `on activate` fails before `auth.submit` would otherwise never unlock. The change to spec.md 8.3 and 12 adds no syntax and keeps every accepted program accepted with the meaning 8.3 already gave it (section 14). Tests, each failing with the fix taken out: `crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::a_failed_await_in_a_handler_stops_no_other_handler` (a failed exit, a result that does not read as `int`, a division by zero, each reported unfrozen, a plain box clicked after each and the failed one again), `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_handlers_error_freezes_nothing` (the component's timer and other handler run on; a binding's fault in it still freezes it).

## ipc-large-answer

**2026-11-08 · ipc-large-answer: an IPC answer of any size is delivered; the 1 MiB cap drops only a client that leaves that much unread.** `strand get` of a news list holding its entries' HTML (over 1 MiB as JSON) failed with "no answer: the shell closed the connection", and the shell logged that the client did not read its events: `Server::send` appended the line and then dropped the client once its queue passed `MAX_QUEUED`, so a single answer over the cap was dropped before a byte was written. The cap exists for clients that do not read (a paused `strand watch`), so it now looks at what is still unread from earlier lines when a new one comes: a client more than 1 MiB behind is dropped, and a line of any size is queued whole and written as the client reads. Refusing a large answer with a message naming its size was the other choice; it was not taken because a value the shell already holds in memory (an action's output is itself capped at 4 MiB) is a legitimate thing to read, and a limit there would be a second concept a builder has to know, for no protection the unread cap does not already give: the memory a stalled client can hold is at most the cap plus one line. The client side reads lines of any length. Test, failing without the fix: `crates/strand/src/ipc/server.rs::tests::an_answer_over_the_cap_is_delivered_and_a_stalled_watcher_dropped` (a 3 MiB answer arrives whole and the line after it too; a watcher that reads nothing is still dropped).

## build-ready-date

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-date: a `Date` no source has filled is 1970-01-01, and a date without a time of day formats as its midnight.** A `Date` field's default was the record of its fields' defaults, year, month and day 0, which is no date: `feed.at.format("%b %d")` before the feed answered was the runtime fault "not a date", which freezes its component outlined in red until a reload (spec.md 12), so the component stayed red after the data came. The fault, not the freeze, was the fault: spec.md 12 keeps a binding's fault frozen until a reload, deliberately (a component that recovers on its own would hide a broken binding), so the fix is that a missing value is no error. The default `Date` is now 1970-01-01 with `hour` and `minute` null (chrono's `NaiveDate::default`, `vm::builtins::default_of`), a date every `Date` method works on, as `0` and `""` are values every number and text method works on; `Date?`, which the docs recommend where a source may leave a date out, stays null. Second, `format` with an hour or minute pattern (`%H:%M`) on a date without a time of day was the fault "cannot format this value"; document dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`, an RSS feed's day) make such dates common. It now formats as that day's midnight, `00:00`, as Python's `date.strftime` does, which matches how such a date already orders (before every time that day, m6-w2-language); `time_of` already read a null minute as 0. Rejected: formatting a date-only value's hour as empty text (a third rule for one method), and a valid default only for `format` (`add` and `month_start` would still fault). `Date` is a `provisional` schema record, and no accepted program changes meaning except that two faults are gone (spec.md 5.6's doc-formats bullet amended under section 14) (`crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::an_unfilled_date_formats_and_a_date_only_one_formats_midnight`, failing without the fix).

## build-ready-file-palette

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-file-palette: a `file`'s scope `text:` that reads a token waits for the palette.** A `template:` file waits for the palette with no fallback (`Ctx::palette_ok`) and for a wallpaper still being quantised, but a scope `text:` resolved its tokens through the token table built over the fallback palette (`VmHooks::token`), so a generated theme file (kitty colours from `join(…, hex($fg))`) was written once with the fallback's colours, its `run:` ran, and then again with the real ones. Counting token reads in the hook misses a `let` of a token that another reader (a label) already worked out, since its memo answers without calling the hook; a static walk of the text's dependency graph in the compiler would have to follow every `let`, `fn` and component argument. The runtime already has that graph: `Runtime::reads_so_far` (new) gives what the running content memo has read, and `Ctx::read_the_palette` walks those nodes' `sources` for the token table's or the palette's memo. Only when the palette is not settled (`Ctx::palette_settled`: `palette_ok` and no image pending, read untracked first so a file reading no token gains no dependency) is the walk made, and a text that reaches either waits (`Content::Pending`), reading the settled state tracked so it is worked out again when the palette is, even if its table comes out the same; a broken palette is the output's error, as for a template. A text that reads no token is written at once. A `Value::Token` text now waits for a pending image too, as a template does (`crates/strand-compiler/tests/outputs.rs::a_scope_text_reading_a_token_waits_for_the_palette`: `join` with `hex($fg)`, a `let` a bar label already read, and a plain text written at once; failing without the fix).

## build-ready-slow-wait

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-slow-wait: a `file` waiting on a service that is up but silent is a notice after 10 s.** live-files made a waiting `file`'s notice name a service with no run up only; one that is up and not ready, such as a declared `from dbus` service whose daemon is absent (it is never ready, service-ready), or a poll whose command never succeeds (build-ready-poll), left a builder with nothing written and no reason. A wait that goes on for `SLOW_WAIT` (10 s, past any first poll or bus read on a working system) is now a standing notice, "waits for `x`, which has not answered in 10 s (a `from dbus` service waits for its daemon); nothing is written until it answers", on the overlay, the log and `strand watch` (a later watcher hears it, as every output notice), given once per wait and gone when the write lands. A wait for another first service starts the count again; a wait with a no-run-up notice is not told twice. The logic loop wakes for it at its deadline (`Files::wait`), with no polling. spec.md 9.7's "one that is up but not ready … waits for it with no notice" is amended under section 14 (a notice, no change of meaning) (`crates/strand/src/run/outputs.rs::tests::a_long_wait_on_a_service_that_is_up_is_a_notice`).

## build-ready-poll

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-poll: a failing `from poll` command is a diagnostic under the service's name, and a poll that never answered is not ready.** A command that exited non-zero, timed out or printed more than a document was a log line naming the program, "`curl` failed (exit status: 22)", with no service and no `ServiceDiagnostic`, so `strand watch` never showed it and a recipe of five `curl` services could not tell which feed failed; and the service turned `ready` after that failed first poll, so a `file` waiting for it wrote defaults and an `if !svc.ready` placeholder vanished. `poll_command` now returns why it failed, and `run_poll` raises it with `Cx::warn` (logged as "service `blog` failed: `curl` failed (exit status: 22)", sent to `strand watch`), once until a poll answers, which resolves it with `Cx::resolve`. spec.md 5.6 defines `ready` as "has answered": a poll service is ready after its first poll that answers; a failed first poll ends the first frame's hold (`ready` then `unready`, as a `from dbus` service with no daemon does), so a dead feed never delays the shell. A poll that fails after one answered keeps its values and stays ready, since they are still its last answer. For the resolution to reach the host, a failure now resolves as a notice does: `ClientInner::open_failure` holds the failure reported, and a later run's `Cx::ready` resolves one a run's end raised, `Cx::resolve` or a clean end any, and another failure replaces it (resolving the old); a resolved failure clears the dedupe, so the same failure after a recovery is news again. A file poll's missing file still reads as no document and is ready, as before (`crates/strand-services/tests/custom.rs::a_failing_poll_is_reported_under_its_name_and_is_not_ready`, failing without the fix; excluded from the CI retry in `.config/nextest.toml`, since it asserts no second report).

## build-ready-notices

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-notices: a `strand watch` that starts later hears the service diagnostics still open.** Service diagnostics (a field that does not convert, a page that is not XML, a failing poll, a run that failed) were broadcast to the watchers connected when they were taken; the usual flow, start the shell and then run `strand watch`, saw nothing of a field broken from the start, though the site says `strand watch` reports it. `Shell::service_open` now keeps each unresolved diagnostic by its service and message (at most 64, the oldest going first; the log has all), takes it out when it is resolved (build-ready-poll makes failures resolvable, and field reports already were), and `watch_request` sends them after the `watching` line with the main thread's and the `file` outputs' standing notices. A reload does not repeat them to watchers already there, which heard them (`crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::open_service_diagnostics_reach_watchers_that_come_later`, failing without the fix; `crates/strand/src/run/shell.rs::open_tests::open_service_diagnostics_are_kept_until_resolved`).

## build-ready-popup

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-popup: a content-sized surface's pass asks for its wrapping texts' layouts at their width.** On sway 1.9 (`xdg_wm_base` 2, the CI image's), a popup holding wrapping text never mapped: it was destroyed and made again every frame, 100% CPU and thousands of wlroots configure errors. The pass that sizes a content-sized surface (`Renderer::refresh_specs`) measures a wrapping text's height from its layout at the box's width when one is shaped, and estimates it from the unbounded layout's line height otherwise (late-text-dip); only the drawn pass asked for the fitted layout, and the pass kept only unbounded layouts alive (`spec_wanted`). So with no surface drawing the popup its height was the estimate (56 px at 14 px text), drawn it was the shaped height (54), and an `xdg_wm_base` below 3 cannot reposition a popup, so each change made it again, with no surface, at the estimate. A compositor that repositions (sway 1.12, Hyprland) moved it once and settled. `natural_texts` now also asks for each text's layout at its content box's width when that is narrower than its unbounded layout (the same condition and width as drawing it, `place_text`), so the size no longer depends on a surface drawing it; on sway 1.9 the popup is made at most once more and maps. Rejected: having the surface manager refuse to remake a popup at a size it was made at before (it would leave a popup at a wrong size when content really toggles), since the cause was the measure, not the remake (`crates/strand-render/tests/popups.rs::a_wrapping_popup_asks_for_one_height_drawn_or_not`, failing without the fix at 14 px: 58 asked undrawn, 56 drawn; seen on headless sway 1.9 with the sweep's config: one remake, mapped, no CPU after).

## build-ready-install

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-install: the install page says the site follows `main`, and gives the edge command.** The site deploys from `main`, and the install command it documents installs the newest release, v0.1.0 (920049b0), which fails `strand check` on the examples of 11 of the 22 pages that have `strand file=` blocks (document formats, the blocks); edge passes all of them. Until a newer release is tagged (docs/development.md, "Releasing", an owner's step), `site/start/install.md` says that a release can be older than the pages and gives `--edge` beside the default command; the sentence stays true after a release, so it needs no edit when one comes.

## build-ready-failures

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-failures: a service's open failure goes when a reload changes or removes the service, or once a later run has stayed up 30 s; a one-off warning is not kept.** The review of build-ready found three ways a service diagnostic stayed open after it stopped holding, so a later `strand watch` kept printing it. A poll's failure was raised with `Cx::warn` and recorded as the live run's, which a later run's readiness did not resolve; `Client::restart` (a reload changing the declaration) and `Client::stop_now` (a reload removing it) resolved only notices, so fixing a feed's URL and saving left "service `blog`: `curl` failed (exit status: 22)" open, and the dedupe (`last_error`) then dropped the same failure after the fix. Now a restart, a stop for good and the stop after the last reader leaves resolve every open diagnostic and clear the dedupe (`ClientInner::resolve_all`), and the open failure records which run raised it (`open_failure`'s run number), so a later run resolves it. Second, build-ready-poll resolved a run's end failure as soon as the next run said it was ready, which broke the dedupe for a run that fails right after its first read (a `from listen` command exiting at once, a daemon crashing after its properties are read): every backoff cycle logged a resolved and a failed line, about every 30 s forever. A later run now resolves an earlier failure only once it has stayed up `RETRY_MAX` (30 s) since it started (`ClientInner::arm_settle`, one timer per run), the same mark the backoff and the dedupe already use for a run that stayed up; a service that recovers is said to be resolved 30 s later, and a reload's restart resolves at once. Third, `Cx::warn` also carries one-off events (polkit's conversation failing after an answer, the clipboard unable to keep an image), and keeping those for later watchers replayed them as if current. `Cx::warn` is now the one-off kind again, as before build-ready (`ServiceDiagnostic::standing` false: logged and sent to the watchers there, not kept), and the new `Cx::failing` is the standing kind a run resolves with `Cx::resolve`, used by `from poll`; every other diagnostic (a run's end, a notice, a field that does not convert) is standing. Rejected: a time limit on kept diagnostics (a failure that still holds would vanish), and making each builtin's `warn` sites choose (most are events, and the one standing user is the poll). Also from the review: a poll whose first poll failed while its reader went hidden was made ready at the loop's top, though no poll had answered; that check now also requires that no failed first poll ended the hold. spec.md 12's service-failure paragraph says when a failure is resolved (section 14: no syntax, no change of meaning for an accepted program). Tests, each failing without its part: `crates/strand-services/tests/contract.rs::{a_restart_or_a_stop_resolves_a_live_runs_failure, an_earlier_runs_failure_is_resolved_once_a_later_run_stays_up, a_body_failing_right_after_ready_is_reported_once}`, `crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::a_reload_that_fixes_or_removes_a_service_takes_its_failure_away`, `crates/strand/src/run/shell.rs::open_tests::open_service_diagnostics_are_kept_until_resolved` (a one-off is not kept), `crates/strand-services/tests/custom.rs::a_failed_first_poll_hidden_meanwhile_is_still_not_ready`.

## handler-fault-repeat

**2026-11-08 · handler-fault-repeat: a handler failing the same way again is reported once, until a run of it completes.** handler-fault stopped freezing a component for a handler's error, which also removed the only limit on repeats: the first fault used to freeze the component and so stop its timer. An `every 2s { cpu = await sensors() }` whose command prints text where an `int` is read, or a `1 / zero` in an `every 100ms`, then wrote an ERROR line and a `strand watch` `fault` per tick (36,000 an hour at 100 ms, measured 75 in 7.5 s on headless sway), burying what a builder reads. The `reporting` wrapper every `on`, `after` and `every` body runs in now keeps, per handler (`Site::reported`), the error text its last failing run reported: a run failing with the same text is not reported, a run that completes clears it, so the next failure is reported again, and a different error is reported at once. This keeps spec.md 8.3's rule that nothing is frozen and the handler runs at every event. A click that fails the same way twice is reported once, which is what the log already said; the handler still runs each time. Rejected: a rate limit on the clock (a failure every 61 s would still be one line a minute forever, and tests would need the clock), and counting repeats in a later line (no natural moment to say it, since the handler may never complete). spec.md 8.3 gains the sentence (section 14: no syntax, no change of meaning). Tests, failing without the fix: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_handler_failing_the_same_way_is_reported_once_until_a_run_completes` (an `every` dividing by zero is one fault over four ticks, another handler's error is its own, a completed run makes the next failure news); `a_handlers_error_freezes_nothing` and `crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::a_failed_await_in_a_handler_stops_no_other_handler` now prove the second run of the failing handler by its write, not by a second fault.

## build-ready-slow-wait-gone

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-slow-wait-gone: a `file` a reload removes or moves while it waits is let go.** build-ready-slow-wait's entries (`Files::slow`) and live-files' no-run-up waits (`Files::waiting`) were removed only by an `OutputChange` for the same path, and a removed `file`, or one whose path changed, makes none, so 10 s after the wait began a notice came, on the overlay, the log and every later `strand watch`, for a path no longer in the config, and stayed until a restart. `Files::keep`, run after every diff, now lets go of the waits whose path `Instance::output_targets` no longer lists, whether or not the writer thread has started (a `file` that only ever waited never started it), and the shell takes those paths' notices and overlay rows away (`output_ok`). Tests, failing without the fix: `crates/strand/src/run/outputs.rs::tests::a_wait_whose_file_is_gone_is_let_go` (`Files::let_go` itself) and, added in the last review round because nothing failed with the call in `Files::keep` taken out, `::keep_lets_go_of_the_waits_no_file_writes` (`Files::keep` on an instance whose only `file` is another path).

## handler-fault-repeat-watch

**2026-11-08 · handler-fault-repeat-watch: a `strand watch` started after a handler's repeated fault hears it at the handler's next failing run.** handler-fault-repeat reports a handler's error once until a run of it completes, but faults are events, not standing notices, so they were never replayed to a later watcher: an `every 100ms { n = 1 / zero }` failing since boot printed nothing to a `strand watch` opened 3 s in (headless sway, release build at 89d519d1), while site/help/troubleshooting.md tells a builder to open `strand watch` and read the `fault:` line, which is the usual order. Each `strand watch` that starts now calls `Instance::report_faults_again`, which bumps the instance's fault epoch; `Site::reported` keeps the epoch with the error text, so the same error in a later epoch is reported once more, then deduped again. A watcher therefore hears a still-failing handler at its next failing run (the next tick for a timer, the next click for a click handler). Watchers that were already listening hear it a second time, which is one extra line per new watch, not one per tick. Rejected: keeping handler faults open and replaying them at subscribe as service_open does, because a handler's fault has no moment at which it is resolved (the handler may never run again), so a click that failed once an hour ago would be replayed to every later watcher as if still current, which is the stale kind of notice build-ready-failures removed for one-off warnings; and clearing every handler's `reported` (no epoch), which would also mean walking every site. spec.md 8.3 gains the clause. Tests, failing without the fix: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/instantiate.rs::a_handler_failing_the_same_way_is_reported_once_until_a_run_completes` (after `report_faults_again` the same failure is one more fault, then none) and `crates/strand/src/run/tests.rs::a_late_watch_hears_a_handler_still_failing_the_same_way` (a socket watch subscribing after the dedupe hears the next failing click, both watchers then hear the one after that as nothing; each step is read up to a host notice sent after it, not a quiet window).

## lock-fault-epoch

**2026-11-08 · lock-fault-epoch: a handler's repeated fault is reported again in each lock session.** handler-fault-repeat drops a handler's error when it is the same as the last one, with no completed run between (`Site::reported`). The lock's own logic (its `on change`, service handlers and timers, `lock::lock_logic`) is mounted once and only suspended between locks, so its sites kept `reported` from one lock to the next: a lock whose password goes through such a handler (`on change asked { await auth.submit(pw) }`) and fails the same way in a later lock (no helper, a PAM error) never reached `ctx.errors`, so `lock_faults` never showed the built-in password field and that lock could not be unlocked. That is the lockout `lock_faults` is there to prevent. A lock session that begins (the lock's `open` turning true after the last session ended, or `Locked` after `Ended`) now bumps the instance's fault epoch, as a new `strand watch` does (handler-fault-repeat-watch), so the first such failure in each lock is reported. Within one lock it is still reported once. Rejected: skipping the dedupe while a lock is shown (a timer failing each tick would flood the log during a lock), and letting `lock_faults` see deduped errors (a second path for errors the rest of the shell does not see). Test, failing without the fix: `crates/strand-compiler/tests/lock.rs::a_lock_logic_failure_is_reported_again_in_the_next_lock`.

## build-ready-standing

**2026-11-08 · build-ready-standing: the adapter's fallback and a missing `strand-auth` helper are standing diagnostics.** The build-ready review made `Cx::warn` a one-off (`standing: false`, not kept in `Shell::service_open`), but two conditions that hold for as long as the run does still used it: the compositor adapter falling back to the standard protocols (`wm/service.rs`, `Sources::degraded`, which holds until the adapter understands the compositor again) and `auth` finding no `strand-auth` helper (looked up once per run). A `strand watch` started after boot, the flow the site documents, heard neither. Both are now `Cx::failing`; the store that raised the degradation resolves it (`Cx::resolve`) when `degraded` clears, and a store that becomes the one that reports (the older one left) raises what still holds. `AuthConfig::find_helper` (default `strand_auth::default_helper`) lets a test run with none installed. `Cx::warn` stays for one-off events: a copied image not kept, a password that could not be checked. Tests, failing without the fix: `crates/strand-services/tests/wm_services.rs::a_hyprland_the_adapter_cannot_read_falls_back_to_the_protocols_with_a_diagnostic` (the degradation is standing and resolved once Hyprland is understood again) and `crates/strand-services/tests/auth.rs::auth_checks_through_the_helper_and_only_success_unlocks` (no helper: one standing diagnostic, not resolved while the store runs).

## outputs-frame

**2026-11-08 · outputs-frame: an apply Hyprland holds for a frame is given one.** Hyprland 0.57 saves a configuration's state at `apply` and runs the monitor rule reload, which applies it and sends `succeeded`, in its next render's pre-checks (`CMonitorRuleManager::scheduleReload` only sets a flag; `OutputManagement.cpp` queues the success until `stateReloaded`). An idle desktop renders nothing, so an apply sent while nothing moved waited for the pointer. On nested Hyprland with the monitor-profiles page, a live edit waited 13 s, the applies behind it ran one change late, and after a hotplug the earlier set's layout briefly showed. main's edge build does the same. The outputs service now binds `wl_compositor`, `wl_shm` and the layer shell on its own connection, and when an apply is unanswered for 100 ms it shows a 1x1 fully transparent layer surface (namespace `strand-outputs`, overlay layer, empty input region, no keyboard, no exclusive zone), commits it again every 500 ms while the answer does not come, and destroys it once it does. Each commit damages the screen, so Hyprland draws a frame and applies the configuration. sway, niri and labwc answer at once, so they get one only for an apply they take over 100 ms to answer (a slow modeset), where it is harmless (it shows nothing and takes no input; the service does not check which compositor it is on). Rejected: asking Hyprland for a frame over its IPC (no request does only that; `hyprctl reload` and the dispatchers that damage every monitor also reset input or monitor rules), a zero-move virtual pointer (another protocol and a fake input event), committing one of the shell's own surfaces (a config may have none, and it would tie the service to strand-surface), and only documenting it (a builder would see profiles apply late with nothing to act on). On nested Hyprland 0.57 with the page's config and no pointer motion, every idle edit was answered about 2 ms after the surface's first commit, about 100 ms after the apply, and a restarted shell's first apply too. strand-fake-wayland gains `FakeBuilder::applies_at_frame`: Hyprland's shapes hold each configuration's reload and `succeeded` until any client commits a surface that draws. Test, failing without the fix: `crates/strand-services/tests/outputs.rs::an_apply_waiting_for_a_frame_is_given_one`.

**2026-11-08 · outputs-frame final round: an apply waiting with no frame surface to make does not spin.** The time of the last frame was kept on the surface, so when the surface could not be made (a compositor offering the output manager without `wl_shm` or the layer shell, or a failed `memfd_create`), the next frame was due at the apply's send time plus 100 ms, already past, and the service's `poll` ran with no timeout left until the answer came: a whole core for as long as an apply went unanswered. The time of the last try (`Client::nudged`) is now kept whether or not a surface was made, so the next try is 500 ms later; a surface the compositor closes is made again 500 ms later too, not at once. None of sway, niri, labwc or Hyprland was affected.
